correctness.rationale: Read entire RESULT.md and verify_cyclic_good.py. Baranwal et al Theorem11 gives the minimal antisquare basis, and Proposition18 shows a bi-infinite good word with 001011 must be a nonperiodic one-defect word, excluding it and its reversal/complement on any period. Thus periodic good words are exactly eight-factor avoiders. Cyclic XOR difference p maps those eight to 010,101,11111,01110. Any nonzero good p consists of alternating 0-runs length>=2 and 1-runs length2 or4; total number of ones is even, yielding two lifts to bits. With block GF B=z²/(1-z)*(u²z²+u⁴z⁴), marking 1-run starts yields 2n/r * [z^n u^t]B^r, i.e. F=-2z*d_z log(1-z-u²z⁴-u⁴z⁶). Coefficient extraction proves full bivariate finite sum; rotation stabilizers are handled by marked position double counting. Periodic inversion yields primitive necklace a_n=(1/n)sum mu(d)g_(n/d), and factoring denominator (1+z³)(1-z-z³) gives growth 2psi^n+O(1). Fresh independent exhaustive 8190 periodic binary words lengths1..12 were tested for true antisquares up to sufficient order and the four differences and rational census; source checker independently covers n1..15. Neither finite range implies all-n result, which follows from cited structural rigidity and run counting.

value.rationale: A complete multivariate census by circumference and number of cyclic transitions for a natural symbolic-dynamics language of good antisquare-free infinite periodic points is a useful exact invariant; it also determines all primitive and imprimitive necklaces. This extends published linear-word asymptotic growth information to exact periodic-point zeta-type data, not just an arbitrary finite table.
